title: Diabetic and Endocrine Emergencies: D10W and the PCP Order

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already check blood glucose, give oral glucose and give glucagon. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Explain why low sugar, DKA and HHS happen, and tell them apart
  2. Run the BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol at PCP level, with D10W
  3. Recognize adrenal and thyroid crises, and support them safely

Textbook: Chapter 32, PDF pages 2895–2945
slides.say: Welcome to class. As EMRs, you've checked blood sugars, put glucose gel in patients' mouths, and given glucagon to patients who couldn't swallow. As a PCP, you get a new tool: an IV and D10W, which is ten percent dextrose, and with it a new order of decisions. Today we'll cover three things. First, the physiology, so you understand why low sugar, DKA and HHS look so different. Second, the BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol at PCP level: when to give D10W, how much, and when glucagon is still your choice. Third, the rarer crises from the adrenal and thyroid glands.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。作为 EMR，你们测过血糖，把葡萄糖凝胶放进病人嘴里，也给不能吞咽的病人打过胰高血糖素。作为 PCP，你多了一个新工具：静脉通路和 D10W，也就是百分之十的葡萄糖，随之而来的是新的决策顺序。今天讲三件事。第一，生理机制，让你明白低血糖、DKA 和 HHS 为什么表现差别这么大。第二，PCP 级别的 BC 糖尿病急症流程：什么时候给 D10W、给多少、什么时候还是选胰高血糖素。第三，比较少见的肾上腺和甲状腺危象。

slides.title: Insulin and glucagon: the see-saw
slides.body:
Insulinbeta cells; lowers glucosethe only hormone that does
Glucagonalpha cells; raises glucoseliver glycogen → sugar
Braindepends on glucoselow sugar = starving brain
  • Type 1: makes almost no insulin; stopping it → DKA
  • Type 2: mostly insulin resistance; diet, pills, sometimes insulin
  • The type depends on insulin dependence, not age
slides.say: Let's start with the see-saw. In the pancreas, beta cells make insulin, which moves sugar into the cells and lowers blood glucose. It's the only hormone that lowers glucose. Alpha cells make glucagon, which tells the liver to turn its stored glycogen back into sugar. Most organs can burn fat or protein, but the brain depends on glucose, so low sugar means a starving brain. In type one diabetes, the body makes almost no insulin, so the patient needs it every day, and stopping it can cause DKA. Type two is mostly insulin resistance, treated with diet, exercise, pills and sometimes insulin. The type depends on insulin dependence, not on age.
slides.sayZh: 先讲跷跷板。胰腺里的 β 细胞分泌胰岛素，把糖送进细胞，降低血糖；它是唯一能降血糖的激素。α 细胞分泌胰高血糖素，让肝脏把储存的糖原重新变成糖。大多数器官能烧脂肪或蛋白质，但大脑依赖葡萄糖，所以低血糖就是大脑在挨饿。1 型糖尿病身体几乎不产胰岛素，病人每天都要用，一停就可能发生 DKA。2 型主要是胰岛素抵抗，靠饮食、运动、口服药，有时也用胰岛素。分型看是否依赖胰岛素，不看年龄。

slides.title: Hypoglycemia: a starving brain
slides.body:
BC protocol: treat BGL < 4.0 mmol/L

  • Causes: too much insulin or pills, too little food, extra exercise
  • Adrenaline signs: shaky, sweaty, fast pulse, hungry
  • Brain signs: confusion, slurred speech, aggression, seizure, coma
  • Onset in minutes; can look drunk or like a stroke
  • Severe for over 30 min → risk of permanent brain damage
slides.say: Hypoglycemia usually comes from too much insulin or diabetes pills, too little food, or both, and unusual exercise without enough food adds to it. Normal blood glucose is about four to eight millimoles per litre, and the BC protocol treats a level below four point zero. The signs come in two groups. The adrenaline group: shaking, sweating, a fast pulse and hunger. The brain group: confusion, slurred speech, poor coordination, aggression, seizures and coma. It starts within minutes and can look like drunkenness or even a stroke. Severe hypoglycemia lasting more than thirty minutes can cause permanent brain damage.
slides.sayZh: 低血糖通常来自胰岛素或降糖药用多了、吃得太少，或两者都有；不寻常的运动又没吃够东西也会加重。正常血糖约四到八毫摩尔每升，BC 流程规定低于四点零就要处理。征象分两组。肾上腺素组：发抖、出汗、心跳快、饥饿。大脑组：意识混乱、言语含糊、动作不协调、有攻击性、抽搐和昏迷。它在几分钟内发生，看起来像喝醉，甚至像卒中。严重低血糖持续超过三十分钟，可能造成永久性脑损伤。

slides.title: Too high: DKA versus HHS
slides.body:
DKAHHS
Whotype 1; teens, young adultstype 2; older; ~30% undiagnosed
Glucose (book)above about 18 mmol/Labove about 33 mmol/L
Coursebuilds over 12–48 hillness + poor drinking (pneumonia, UTI)
Key signsKussmaul breathing, fruity breath, vomitingsevere dehydration, confusion, stroke-like signs
Ketonesyesno significant ketones
slides.say: When sugar runs high, two emergencies matter. DKA, or diabetic ketoacidosis, mostly hits type one diabetics. Without insulin the cells starve, so the body burns fat, which makes acids and ketones. Sugar spills into the urine and drags water with it, so the patient dries out. Look for deep, fast Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, vomiting, and warm, dry skin. It builds over twelve to forty-eight hours. HHS, or hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome, is usually type two and older, often after an illness like pneumonia. The sugar is even higher, there are no significant ketones, and the patient is severely dehydrated, often confused or with stroke-like signs. About thirty percent didn't know they had diabetes.
slides.sayZh: 血糖过高时，有两种急症要关注。DKA，即糖尿病酮症酸中毒，多见于 1 型糖尿病人。没有胰岛素，细胞挨饿，身体就去烧脂肪，产生酸和酮体。糖漏进尿里，把水一起带走，病人就脱水了。要找深快的 Kussmaul 呼吸、呼气有果味、呕吐、皮肤温暖干燥。它在十二到四十八小时内逐渐形成。HHS，即高渗性高血糖综合征，多是 2 型、年纪较大，常在肺炎这类疾病之后发生。血糖更高，没有明显的酮症，病人严重脱水，常有意识混乱或类似卒中的表现。约百分之三十的人此前不知道自己有糖尿病。

slides.q: A 17-year-old with type 1 diabetes has vomited for two days. He breathes deep and fast, his breath smells fruity, and his skin is warm and dry. He is drowsy but answers you. What is most likely?
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A seventeen-year-old with type one diabetes has vomited for two days. He breathes deep and fast, his breath smells fruity, and his skin is warm and dry. He's drowsy but answers you. What is most likely? A, hypoglycemia. B, diabetic ketoacidosis, or DKA. C, hyperosmolar hyperglycemic syndrome, or HHS. D, hyperventilation from anxiety. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你。一位十七岁的 1 型糖尿病人呕吐两天了，呼吸深而快，呼气有果味，皮肤温暖干燥，嗜睡但能回答你。最可能是什么？A 低血糖；B 糖尿病酮症酸中毒，即 DKA；C 高渗性高血糖综合征，即 HHS；D 焦虑引起的过度通气。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, DKA. A young type one patient, a slow build over days, Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath from ketones, and warm, dry skin is the classic picture. Hypoglycemia comes on in minutes, with pale, sweaty skin. HHS is mostly older type two patients without significant ketones, so no fruity breath. Anxiety can cause fast breathing, but not ketone breath or two days of vomiting. Still check the glucose; it's quick, and it supports your picture.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，DKA。年轻的 1 型病人、几天内慢慢形成、Kussmaul 呼吸、酮体带来的果味、皮肤温暖干燥，这是典型表现。低血糖几分钟内发生，皮肤苍白出汗；HHS 多见于年纪大的 2 型病人，没有明显酮症，所以没有果味；焦虑可以让呼吸变快，但不会有酮味，也不会呕吐两天。血糖还是要测，测得快，也能印证你的判断。

slides.title: High sugar: what the PCP does
slides.body:
• Airway first; suction ready, they vomit
  • Oxygen, glucose check, stroke check
  • Shock from fluid loss → Hypovolemia protocol: 20 mL/kg, max 2 L
  • Reassess every 500 mL; listen to the lungs
  • No insulin on the BC exam; it waits for hospital

Book: potassium can swing high or low fast; peaked T waves suggest it is high.
slides.say: So what do you do for high sugar? Insulin isn't on the BC licensing exam, and the book also says it should wait for hospital, where the levels can be checked. Your job is the ABCs and the fluid. Protect the airway and keep suction ready, because these patients vomit. Give oxygen, check the glucose, and look for stroke signs. They're often badly dehydrated; in HHS the fluid deficit can be ten litres or more. If they're in shock from fluid loss, the PCP uses the BC hypovolemia protocol: twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and listening to the lungs. The book also warns that potassium can swing high or low quickly.
slides.sayZh: 那高血糖怎么处理？胰岛素执照考试不考，书里也说胰岛素应该留到医院，在那里能监测各项指标。你的任务是 ABC 和补液。保护气道，备好吸引，因为这些病人会呕吐。给氧、测血糖、查卒中征象。他们常常严重脱水，HHS 的缺液量可以达到十升以上。如果因体液丢失而休克，PCP 按 BC 低血容量流程：每公斤二十毫升、最多两升，每五百毫升复评，并听诊肺部。书里还提醒，血钾可能很快地忽高忽低。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: BC Diabetic Emergencies
slides.body:
Known diabetics with decreased LOC, or decreased LOC with no known cause

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway, O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%, side position if needed
  • History, vitals and BGL; check for stroke
  • BGL < 4.0 and can protect airway → oral glucose
  • EMR: can't protect airway → glucagon

PCP adds

  • IV access
  • Confirmed low: D10W 10–25 g (100–250 mL)
  • Glucagon only if you can't get an IV
  • Transport after the first dose of D10W or glucagon
slides.say: Here's the BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol. Every licence level manages the airway, gives oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, positions the patient on the side if needed, gets a history, vitals and a glucose, and checks for stroke. With a glucose below four point zero, a patient who can protect the airway gets oral glucose. At EMR level, a patient who can't protect the airway gets glucagon. The PCP column changes that order: start an IV and correct confirmed hypoglycemia with D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. Glucagon becomes your backup when there's no IV. Then transport after the first dose.
slides.sayZh: 这是 BC 的糖尿病急症流程。各级别都要：管理气道，给氧使血氧达到九十四以上，必要时侧卧，取得病史、生命体征和血糖，并查卒中征象。血糖低于四点零、能自己保护气道的病人，给口服葡萄糖。EMR 级别遇到不能保护气道的病人，给胰高血糖素。PCP 这一栏改变了顺序：开静脉，用 D10W 十到二十五克纠正已证实的低血糖；胰高血糖素变成开不了静脉时的备选。给完第一剂后就转运。

slides.title: D10W: your new drug
slides.body:
D10WBC monograph
LicencePCP (IV only)
Indicationshypoglycemia; altered responsiveness; coma or seizure not yet diagnosed
Contraindicationsnone
Dose10–25 g IV = 100–250 mL of 10%
Onsetimmediate
Cautionleaks out of the vein → tissue necrosis
slides.say: Let's look closely at D10W, ten percent dextrose in water. It's a PCP drug, because it goes into a vein. Every one hundred millilitres holds ten grams of sugar, so the BC dose of ten to twenty-five grams is one hundred to two hundred fifty millilitres. It works immediately. The indications are suspected or known hypoglycemia, an altered level of responsiveness, and coma or seizure not yet diagnosed, and the monograph lists no contraindications. The big caution is extravasation, which means the fluid leaking out of the vein into the tissue, where it can kill that tissue. So make sure the line flows freely before you run it, and watch the site while it runs.
slides.sayZh: 仔细看看 D10W，百分之十的葡萄糖水溶液。它是 PCP 用药，因为要走静脉。每一百毫升含十克糖，所以 BC 的剂量十到二十五克，就是一百到二百五十毫升。它即刻起效。适应证是疑似或已知低血糖、反应水平改变、原因未明的昏迷或抽搐，药物专论没有列禁忌证。最大的注意事项是外渗，也就是液体从静脉漏到组织里，会让那片组织坏死。所以输之前先确认管路通畅，输的过程中盯住穿刺部位。

slides.title: Oral glucose and glucagon
slides.body:
Oral glucoseGlucagon
Whocan protect own airwayPCP: when IV attempts fail
Dose15 g PO; repeat at 5 min, no limit0.5–1 mg IM, or 3 mg IN
Repeatas neededIN: after 15 min if no response
Timing—onset ~15 min; lasts ~90 min

Can't protect the airway? Nothing by mouth.
slides.say: Your EMR tools still matter. Oral glucose is fifteen grams by mouth, repeated every five minutes as needed with no limit, but only for a patient awake enough to protect their own airway. If they can't protect their airway, nothing goes in the mouth. Glucagon is half to one milligram IM, or three milligrams intranasal, and the intranasal dose can be repeated after fifteen minutes if there's no response. For you as a PCP, it's the backup when IV attempts fail. Why not first? It's slower, taking about fifteen minutes, and it works by releasing sugar stored in the liver, so a patient with little stored sugar may respond poorly. D10W works immediately.
slides.sayZh: 你的 EMR 工具仍然重要。口服葡萄糖十五克，必要时每五分钟重复，不设上限，但只给清醒到能自己保护气道的病人。不能自己保护气道的，嘴里什么都不能放。胰高血糖素是零点五到一毫克肌注，或三毫克经鼻；经鼻给药十五分钟无效可以重复。对 PCP 来说，它是开静脉失败时的备选。为什么不首选？它慢，大约十五分钟才起效，而且靠释放肝脏储存的糖起作用，储存少的病人可能效果差。D10W 则即刻起效。

slides.q: A 58-year-old with diabetes is unresponsive with snoring breathing. BGL is 2.2 mmol/L. You have opened the airway and given oxygen. As the PCP, what comes next?
options: Put glucose gel between his cheek and gum
Start an IV, give D10W 10–25 g, then transport
Give D50W 25 g by IV push
Give glucagon IM first; try an IV only if he doesn't wake
slides.say: A fifty-eight-year-old with diabetes is unresponsive with snoring breathing. His glucose is two point two. You've opened the airway and given oxygen. As the PCP, what comes next? A, put glucose gel between his cheek and gum. B, start an IV, give D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, then transport. C, give D50W, twenty-five grams, by IV push. D, give glucagon IM first, and try an IV only if he doesn't wake. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 一位五十八岁的糖尿病人昏迷不醒，呼吸有鼾声，血糖二点二。你已经开放气道并给氧。作为 PCP，下一步做什么？A 把葡萄糖凝胶放在他的颊部和牙龈之间；B 开静脉，给 D10W 十到二十五克，然后转运；C 静脉推注 D50W 二十五克；D 先肌注胰高血糖素，他不醒再试着开静脉。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. For a PCP, confirmed hypoglycemia is corrected with D10W, ten to twenty-five grams IV, and you transport after the first dose. A is wrong: oral glucose is only for patients who can protect their own airway. C is wrong: D50W isn't on the BC licensing exam; D10W is the only exam IV dextrose. D reverses the PCP order: glucagon is for when you can't get IV access, and it is slower.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。对 PCP 来说，已证实的低血糖用 D10W 十到二十五克静脉纠正，给完第一剂就转运。A 错：口服葡萄糖只给能自己保护气道的病人。C 错：D50W 执照考试不考，考试里唯一的静脉葡萄糖是 D10W。D 把 PCP 的顺序弄反了：胰高血糖素用于开不了静脉的时候，而且起效更慢。

slides.title: After the sugar: reassess and look wider
slides.body:
• Recheck BGL and LOC after every dose
  • Why? Missed meal, insulin change, exercise, alcohol, overdose
  • Check the fridge for insulin; bring all medications
  • Functional enquiry (PCP only) includes the endocrine system
  • Normal sugar, still not waking? Head injury, stroke, seizure, overdose
  • Diabetics can have an MI with no chest pain
slides.say: Getting the sugar up is not the end. Recheck the glucose and the level of consciousness after every dose. Then ask why it happened: a missed meal, a change in insulin, extra exercise, alcohol, or even an intentional overdose. Check the fridge for insulin and bring the medications. Your PCP functional enquiry includes the endocrine system. If the sugar is normal and the patient still isn't waking, think wider: head injury, stroke, seizure or overdose. People with diabetes can also have a heart attack with no chest pain, only weakness or shortness of breath. And if a patient wakes up and wants to stay home, encourage transport for observation, because the sugar may not stay up.
slides.sayZh: 把血糖升上去并不是结束。每给一剂都复查血糖和意识水平。然后问为什么会这样：漏了一餐、胰岛素调整、运动增加、喝酒，甚至是故意过量。查一下冰箱里有没有胰岛素，把药物都带上。PCP 的系统问诊包括内分泌系统。血糖正常了病人还是不醒，就要想得更广：颅脑外伤、卒中、抽搐或药物过量。糖尿病人也可能发生没有胸痛的心肌梗死，只表现为乏力或气短。还有，病人醒了想留在家里，要劝他去医院观察，因为血糖不一定能保持住。

slides.title: Adrenal and thyroid crises
slides.body:
CrisisCluesYour care
Adrenal (Addisonian)shock, vomiting, belly or back pain, confusion; stopped steroidsABCs, glucose, fluid for shock
Myxedema comaolder woman, winter, falling LOC, low temperatureO₂, glucose, passive rewarming; no sedatives
Thyroid stormfever, very fast pulse, agitation, possible heart failuretreat threats, support, nearest ED
slides.say: Now three rarer crises. In an adrenal crisis, also called an Addisonian crisis, the body lacks cortisol, a stress hormone. The main picture is shock, with vomiting, diarrhea, severe belly, back or leg pain, and confusion. The most common cause is stopping steroid medicine, even inhaled steroids. Myxedema coma is severe low thyroid; picture an older woman in winter with a falling level of consciousness and a low temperature. Rewarm passively and avoid sedatives, because her slow metabolism lets drugs build up. Thyroid storm is the opposite: fever, a very fast pulse, agitation and possible heart failure. For all three: ABCs, oxygen, a glucose check, fluid for shock, and prompt transport.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲三种较少见的危象。肾上腺危象，也叫 Addison 危象，是身体缺少皮质醇这种应激激素。主要表现是休克，伴呕吐、腹泻、腹部、腰背或腿部剧痛和意识混乱。最常见的原因是停用类固醇药物，连吸入型类固醇也算。黏液性水肿昏迷是严重的甲状腺功能减退：想象冬天里一位老年女性，意识越来越差，体温很低。用被动复温，避免镇静药，因为她代谢慢，药物会蓄积。甲状腺危象正好相反：发热、心跳很快、烦躁不安，可能心衰。三种情况的处理都是：ABC、给氧、测血糖、休克时补液、及时转运。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• D10W for confirmed BGL < 4.0: measure before you treat
  • Check the IV flows; watch the site, leaked dextrose kills tissue
  • Glucagon is your backup, not your first step
  • Transport after the first dose; reassess en route
  • Fluid: reassess every 500 mL; listen to the lungs
  • "DKA" but deeply unresponsive? Look for another cause
slides.say: Here are the new watch-outs. D10W is for confirmed hypoglycemia, a glucose below four point zero, so measure before you treat. Check that the IV flows freely, and keep watching the site, because dextrose leaking into tissue can kill it. Glucagon is now your backup for when the IV fails, not your first step. Once the first dose of D10W or glucagon is in, start transporting and keep reassessing en route. When you give fluid for dehydration, reassess every five hundred millilitres and listen to the lungs. And if you're thinking DKA but the patient is deeply unresponsive, think again: DKA rarely causes deep coma, so look for another cause.
slides.sayZh: 这些是新的注意事项。D10W 用于已证实的低血糖，也就是血糖低于四点零，所以先测再治。确认静脉通畅，持续观察穿刺部位，因为葡萄糖漏进组织会让组织坏死。胰高血糖素现在是开静脉失败时的备选，不是第一步。第一剂 D10W 或胰高血糖素给完，就开始转运，途中持续复评。为脱水补液时，每五百毫升复评一次并听诊肺部。还有，如果你想到 DKA，病人却深度昏迷，要再想想：DKA 很少导致深昏迷，要找别的原因。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: D50W 12.5–25 g → BC: D10W only, 10–25 g IV
  • BC protocol: one threshold, BGL < 4.0 mmol/L
  • Book: glucagon 1 mg IM → BC: 0.5–1 mg IM or 3 mg IN
  • No insulin on the BC exam
  • Book's sodium bicarbonate and dopamine: not on the exam
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, or 4 mg IN
slides.say: Now the book versus BC. The book pushes D50W, fifty percent dextrose, twelve point five to twenty-five grams. BC has no D50W; the only IV dextrose is D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. The BC protocol gives one threshold, a glucose below four point zero; the book's separate number for newborns isn't in the BC guidelines. The book gives glucagon one milligram IM; the BC dose is half to one milligram IM, or three milligrams intranasal. Insulin isn't on the BC licensing exam, and neither are the book's sodium bicarbonate and dopamine. If you suspect an opioid, ventilate first, then BC naloxone is point four, point four, point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, or four milligrams intranasal.
slides.sayZh: 现在对照书和 BC。书里静推 D50W，也就是百分之五十的葡萄糖，十二点五到二十五克；BC 没有 D50W，唯一的静脉葡萄糖是 D10W，十到二十五克。BC 流程只给一个阈值：血糖低于四点零；书里给新生儿的单独数字在 BC 指南里没有。书里胰高血糖素是一毫克肌注；BC 剂量是零点五到一毫克肌注，或三毫克经鼻。胰岛素执照考试不考，书里的碳酸氢钠和多巴胺也不考。如果怀疑阿片类，先保证通气，然后 BC 的纳洛酮是零点四、零点四、零点八、再两毫克，肌注或静脉，或经鼻四毫克。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Low sugar: BGL < 4.0, minutes, can mimic stroke; DKA/HHS: slow, dry
  2. PCP order: IV + D10W 10–25 g; glucagon if no IV; go after dose one
  3. No insulin, no D50W: airway, glucose, fluid, reassessment

Next: Chapter 33, Allergic Reactions
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: hypoglycemia means a glucose below four point zero; it comes on in minutes and can look like a stroke or drunkenness, while DKA and HHS build slowly and leave the patient dry. Two: the PCP order in BC is an IV and D10W, ten to twenty-five grams, glucagon only if you can't get the IV, and transport after the first dose. Three: insulin and D50W aren't on your licensing exam, so your job is the airway, the glucose, the fluid, and careful reassessment. Next time, Chapter 33, allergic reactions. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，低血糖是血糖低于四点零，几分钟内发生，可以像卒中或喝醉；DKA 和 HHS 慢慢形成，病人是干的。二，BC 的 PCP 顺序：开静脉给 D10W 十到二十五克；开不了静脉才用胰高血糖素；给完第一剂就转运。三，胰岛素和 D50W 执照考试不考，你的任务是气道、血糖、补液和仔细复评。下节课是第 33 章，过敏反应。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
